reason: Both alerts are False Positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) flags the response write at L91-L93, which prints 'result'. 'result' is derived from 'bar'. The 'B' case sets 'bar' to the constant 'bob', filtering out user input 'param'. Thus, the sink value is constant. Alert 2 (java/xml/xpath-injection) flags the expression construction at L82, which uses 'bar'. Following the same logic, 'bar' resolves to 'bob', preventing XPath injection. User input 'param' is effectively neutralized by the hardcoded switch target.
